clause_text: I'm a solo traveler and found Cozumel very easy to navigate.
I just rented a scooter and rode around the island.
The east side is deserted and beautiful.
Roatan was a bit harder to do alone as the taxis are expensive for one person.
I ended up joining a group for a snorkeling trip.
Costa Maya is impossible to enjoy alone without spending a lot of money on a taxi or a tour.
The port area is fine
but everything is priced for tourists.
I'd recommend Cozumel for anyone who likes to explore independently.
We did the Amazing Race excursion in Cozumel and it was a blast!
You have to solve clues and run around the downtown area.
It's a great way to see the city and interact with locals, though you'll be exhausted by the end.
Roatan was much more about nature.
We visited the Iguana farm which was... interesting.
There are hundreds of them everywhere!
It's a bit weird
but definitely unique.
Costa Maya was a bit of a 'meh' day.
We did the fly fishing excursion
but didn't catch anything.
The guide tried hard,
but the fish just weren't biting that day.
Still, it was nice to be out on the water away from the ship crowds.
Costa Maya was a bit of a letdown for me.
The port area feels very manufactured and touristy.
We took a taxi to Mahahual, which was better,
but the vendors there are extremely pushy, making it hard to just relax on the beach.
Cozumel was much better organized.
We did the underwater oxygen helmets and it was a surreal experience seeing the fish so close without needing a SCUBA certification.
Roatan was beautiful
but we had a major delay getting off the ship due to local port authorities, which cut our excursion time short by nearly an hour.
We still managed to see the monkeys and sloths,
but everything felt rushed.
I'd recommend this itinerary for the scenery,
but be prepared for some logistical headaches at the piers.
The ports were nice
but I felt like the excursions were overpriced for what you got.
In Roatan, we paid for a 'private beach' that turned out to be packed with people from three different cruise lines.
The buffet lunch was cold chicken and rice.
Cozumel was better because we just walked to a local pharmacy and then a grocery store to buy real Mexican vanilla and candy.
Much better prices than the 'official' shops.
Costa Maya was fine, we just sat by the port pool.
It's free,
but the drinks are expensive.
The time in port was enough for us, honestly, we were ready to get back to the AC by 2 PM.
Roatan had the best mix of nature and activity.
We did a guided tour that included a viewpoint, local market, and beach stop.
It felt like we saw more of the island beyond the typical tourist spots.
Costa Maya was more hit or miss.
The beach we went to was nice,
but getting there involved some confusion with taxis and timing.
Cozumel was very straightforward.
Good for a relaxed day without much planning.
Roatan ended up being the most memorable stop for us.
We booked a snorkeling trip through a smaller local operator, and the water clarity was unreal.
It didn't feel overly commercial once we got away from the immediate port.
Costa Maya was a bit of a letdown in comparison.
The port area felt like a controlled shopping zone, and we didn't book an excursion, which I think was a mistake.
Cozumel was easier to manage since taxis were straightforward,
but it was definitely the busiest port of the three.
We loved the history in Costa Maya!
The Mayan ruins at Chacchoben are a must-see if you haven't been.
Our guide, Ivan, was so passionate and pointed out spider monkeys in the trees above the temples.
It felt very Indiana Jones.
Cozumel was a bit of a contrast.
We did the Jeep tour around the island.
The east side of the island is much more rugged and beautiful than the side where the ships dock.
No electricity over there, just wild waves and small beach bars.
Roatan was our relaxation day.
We went to Little French Key.
It's a bit pricey to get out there,
but the water is calm and the lunch was fantastic-fresh lobster and coconut rice.
One thing to note: the pier in Roatan is very long, so be prepared for a walk if you don't use the 'magic chair' lift.
Roatan had a solid snorkeling excursion
but the transfer process from ship to boat took longer than expected.
Costa Maya was disappointing without an excursion since we mostly stayed in the port complex and didn't see much else.
Cozumel was more flexible, and we took a taxi to a quieter beach area which ended up being the best part of that stop.
This itinerary really seems to depend on how much you plan ahead.
The ports were a mixed bag.
I loved the history in Costa Maya-the ruins are a must-see even if the drive is long.
Roatan was stunning
but we had a bad experience with a local taxi driver who tried to overcharge us at the end of the day.
It left a bit of a sour taste in my mouth.
Cozumel was the most professional; everything is streamlined for tourists.
We did the submarine tour and it was fascinating to see the reef from 100 feet down.
I think the itinerary is good,
but you have to be careful in Roatan if you aren't on an official ship excursion.
The time spent in each port was mostly okay,
but we felt very rushed in Costa Maya because the ruins tour takes up almost the whole window.
I'd love an extra two hours there just to relax after the long bus ride back.
Cozumel is always a favorite.
We went to Mr. Sanchos for the day.
It's an all-inclusive beach club and they really take care of you.
The food was surprisingly good for a buffet and the drinks kept coming.
It was very crowded though, so if you want peace and quiet, this isn't it.
Roatan was beautiful
but the pier at Coxen Hole is very industrial looking.
We did a catamaran snorkel trip and saw some great coral.
The crew was fun
but the equipment was a bit dated.
Costa Maya was our last stop.
We just walked the pier and did some souvenir shopping.
The walk from the ship to the actual port exit is very long, especially in the heat, so take the little tram if it's running.
Overall, a solid itinerary
but I felt like the port times were a little short for Roatan.
The pacing between ports was interesting.
In Roatan, our excursion had a nice balance between activities and downtime, so we never felt rushed.
Costa Maya felt more rigid.
The ruins tour was informative,
but everything was scheduled tightly and we didn't have much flexibility.
Cozumel gave us the most freedom since we planned our own day,
but it was also the busiest stop.
It took some effort to find a quieter area away from the crowds.
I appreciated that each port offered something different,
but I definitely preferred the more relaxed structure we had in Roatan compared to the more rigid experience in Costa Maya.
Roatan offered the most memorable experience for me.
We joined a small group excursion that combined a wildlife visit and a beach stop, and it felt well paced without being rushed.
Costa Maya was a bit disappointing because we didn't book anything in advance and ended up staying within the port complex, which felt artificial.
Cozumel redeemed things slightly.
We found a quieter beach farther from the main dock area,
but it required negotiating with taxi drivers and figuring out timing to get back.
Overall, I'd say planning ahead is essential for these ports.
I loved the variety on this trip!
Roatan had the best nature-the chocolate factory tour was so cool
the jungle smells amazing after it rains.
Costa Maya was our beach day; we just sat under a palapa in Mahahual and watched the waves.
It was very relaxing, though the seaweed was a bit thick in some spots.
Cozumel was our big excursion day where we went to the San Gervasio ruins.
They aren't as big as the ones on the mainland,
but they were very peaceful and not nearly as crowded.
I felt like we had plenty of time in each port, though I wish Cozumel stayed open a bit later into the evening so we could have had dinner on land.
The transition from the ship to the shore was easy at all three stops, which isn't always the case.
Definitely a solid itinerary for people who like a mix of history and relaxation.
Costa Maya ruins are a must-see!
Chaccoben is amazing.
The jungle setting makes you feel like Indiana Jones.
The guides are very respectful of the history.
Cozumel is better for water sports.
We did a helmet dive which was a unique way to see the reef without needing to know how to scuba.
Roatan was a bit of a mixed bag.
The scenery is 10/10
but the infrastructure is struggling.
We were stuck in a shuttle for 45 minutes just trying to get out of the port area.
Once we got to our destination it was fine,
but the logistics on that island need work.
I went into this cruise mostly interested in cultural experiences, and the ports delivered that unevenly
but still memorably.
Roatan exceeded expectations because we booked a small-group excursion that included a visit to a local community, a short jungle walk, and time near the water.
It felt immersive without being overwhelming.
Costa Maya was more complicated.
The ruins were fascinating and visually striking,
but the long transportation time made the day feel dominated by logistics rather than exploration.
Cozumel, while more commercial, offered flexibility.
We opted out of excursions and created our own plan, which worked well
but required some research beforehand.
I noticed that crowd levels significantly impacted enjoyment, especially in Cozumel where multiple ships were docked.
Overall, I appreciated the variety,
but planning ahead was key to getting the most out of each stop.
Costa Maya was beautiful
but we felt very pressured by the vendors as soon as we stepped off the ship.
We ended up taking a taxi to Mahahual for $4 per person.
It was much more relaxed once we got away from the main cruise terminal.
The beach there is stunning
but the seagrass was a bit heavy the day we visited.
Cozumel was much better for snorkeling; we went to Money Bar and just swam out from the shore.
You don't even need a boat there to see some amazing fish.
Roatan was okay,
but we found the port area quite confusing to navigate and the excursion we had booked was cancelled at the last minute, so we just ended up walking around the local shops which wasn't very exciting.
The itinerary was decent,
but the time in port felt short.
In Cozumel, we barely had enough time to finish our lunch at a local cafe before we had to run back.
Roatan was the highlight; the monkeys at the sanctuary were so fun to interact with.
Costa Maya is a beautiful port, very well-maintained,
but it feels a bit like a movie set rather than a real place in Mexico.
Overall, a good trip,
but I wish we had 2-3 more hours in each location to really explore.
Traveling as a couple, we preferred slower-paced days.
Cozumel worked perfectly for that.
We went to a quieter beach club and spent hours just relaxing.
Roatan was more activity-focused.
We did a combo excursion and felt a bit rushed between stops.
Costa Maya didn't leave much of an impression.
Next time we'd plan something more structured.
We are experienced cruisers so we usually skip the big bus tours.
In Cozumel, we rented a car for the day.
It's very easy to navigate the island as it's basically one big loop.
We found a secluded beach on the east side and had it all to ourselves for two hours.
Just watch out for the moped renters; they drive a bit crazy.
In Costa Maya, we actually stayed in the port and used the pool.
It was crowded
but convenient since we didn't want to deal with a long day.
Roatan was a bit of a struggle.
We tried to do a walking tour
but the hills are very steep and there aren't many sidewalks once you leave the immediate port area.
We ended up just grabbing a taxi back.
If you go to Roatan, definitely plan for transportation.
Don't think you can just wander around on foot like you can in some parts of Cozumel.
The port schedule was okay,
but I wish we had stayed later in Cozumel to see the sunset from the shore.
I'm a solo traveler and I found Roatan very easy to navigate.
I just walked off and found a local driver who took me to West End for $20.
Spent the day at a small cafe on the water and did some great shore snorkeling.
Cozumel was a bit much for me alone-everyone is trying to pull you into their shop or bar.
I ended up going back to the ship after an hour.
Costa Maya was actually quite chill if you stay at the very end of the beach away from the cruise pier.
The food at the local stalls in Mahahual was much better and cheaper than the port food.
I think the time in each port was adequate, though Cozumel feels like it needs a full 12 hours if you want to do the mainland excursions to Tulum.
